subject: y-values scaled or standardized when D~y?

messages.author: 0dbfcf0efe4ff8fe
messages.subject: y-values scaled or standardized when D~y?
parts:
Good day,
I've fit several models where D~y, i.e. density is a linear function of the y-coordinate of the mask, on the link scale.

I would like to be able to predict density at different locations, and particularly model averaged estimates of density at different locations.

By default, predict() and model.average() provide estimates of D for y=0, but of course, 0 is not within the range of actual y-values, which are UTM northings ranging from about 4900000 to 5020000.

I couldn't find an explanation of if or how x- or y-coordinates are scaled in the documentation. I did find mention of scaled y-coordinates in the documentation for PredictDsurface, which "deals automatically with scaling of x- and y-coordinates". When I apply PredictDsurface to my fitted model, values for density are all "NA". Also, I can't easily use predictDsurface to predict model averaged densities(?).

My objective is to determine a set of values for y that I can use in "newdata" to predict density at different locations (just different y-locations), using model.average. Unscaled / unstandardized values are clearly too large. 

If I assume y-coordinates are standardized to a mean of 0 and SD of 1, and use 
> stdvals = seq(from = -1.75, to = 1.75, by = 0.5)
# and
> nd.stdvals = data.frame(bk=c(0,1), g=c("F","M"), session=c(rep("2012", times=8), rep("2018",times=8)), y=rep(stdvals, times=2))
# then
model.average(modlist.FL, realnames = "D", newdata=nd.stdvals, average=c("real"), criterion = c("AICc"), CImethod = c("Wald"))
# seems to yield plausible results.

I was also wondering if using details$centred = T in the call to secr.fit would simplify things?

Thanks in advance,
Eric

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: y-values scaled or standardized when D~y?
parts:
Masks have an attribute 'meanSD' that stores the mean and SD of x- and y- coordinates; these are used to scale the coordinates in density models, pretty much as you have discovered. See e.g. the getcol function embedded in D.designdata (type D.designdata at the R prompt). This is old code that I have barely visited for years...

I apologise for the lack of documentation; there is a little under ?D.designdata, and meanSD is mentioned in a few other places. Also in secr-densitysurfaces I see under Scaling

"secr.fit scales the x- and y-coordinates of mask points to mean = 0, SD = 1 before using the coordinates
in a model. Remember this when you come to use the coefficients of a density model. Functions such as
predictDsurface take care of scaling automatically. predict.secr uses the scaled values (‘newdata’ x = 0,
y = 0), which provides the predicted density at the mask centroid. The mean and SD used in scaling are
those saved as the ‘meanSD’ attribute of a mask (dataframe with columns ‘x’ and ‘y’ and rows ‘mean’ and
‘SD’).

Murray
